source_text: Ζητήσωμεν δέ, εἰ ἐμέλησεν τῷ κυρίῳ προφανερῶσαι περὶ τοῦ ὕδατος καὶ περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ. περὶ μὲν τοῦ ὕδατος γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰσραήλ, πῶς τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ φέρον ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν οὐ μὴ προσδέξονται, ἀλλ’ ἑαυτοῖς οἰκοδομήσουσιν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφήτης: Ἔκστηθι οὐρανέ, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ πλεῖον φριξάτω ἡ γῆ, ὅτι δύο καὶ πονηρὰ ἐποίησεν ὁ λαὸς οὗτος: ἐμὲ ἐγκατέλιπον, πηγὴν ζωῆς, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς ὤρυξαν βόθρον θανάτου. Μὴ πέτρα ἔρημός ἐστιν τὸ ὄρος τὸ ἅγιόν μου Σινᾶ; ἔσεσθε γὰρ ὡς πετεινοῦ νοσσοὶ ἀνιπτάμενοι νοσσιᾶς ἀφῃρημένοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει ὁ προφήτης: Ἐγὼ πορεύσομαι ἔμπροσθέν σου καὶ ὄρη ὁμαλιῶ καὶ πύλας χαλκᾶς συντρίψω καὶ μοχλοὺς σιδηροῦς συγκλάσω, καὶ δώσω σοι θησαυροὺς σκοτεινούς, ἀποκρύφους, ἀοράτους, ἵνα γνῶσιν ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεός. καί: Κατοικήσεις ἐν ὑψηλῷ σπηλαίῳ πέτρας ἰσχυρᾶς. καί: τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ πιστόν: βασιλέα μετὰ δόξης ὄψεσθε, καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ ὑμῶν μελετήσει φόβον κυρίου καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλῳ προφήτῃ λέγει: Καὶ ἔσται ὁ ταῦτα ποιῶν ὡς τὸ ξύλον τὸ πεφυτευμένον παρὰ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὑδάτων, ὃ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ δώσει ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ φύλλον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀπορυήσεται, καὶ πάντα, ὅσα ἂν ποιῇ, κατευοδωθήσεται. οὐχ οὕτως οἱ ἀσεβεῖς, οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλ’ ἢ ὡς ὁ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκρίπτει ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς. διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κρίσει οὐδὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων, ὅτι γινώσκει κύριος ὁδὸν δικαίων, καὶ ὁδὸς ἀσεβῶν ἀπολεῖται. αἰσθάνεσθε, πῶς τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὥρισεν. τοῦτο γὰρ λέγει: μακάριοι, οἲ ἐπὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐλπίσαντες κατέβησαν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ, ὅτι τὸν μὲν μισθὸν λέγει ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ: τότε, φησίν, ἀποδώσω. νῦν δὲ ὅ λέγει: τὰ φύλλα οὐκ ἀπορυήσεται, τοῦτο λέγει: ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξελεύσεται ἐξ ὑμῶν διὰ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἔσται εἰς ἐπιστροφὴν καὶ ἐλπίδα πολλοῖς. καὶ πάλιν ἕτερος προφήτης λέγει. Καὶ ἦν ἡ γῆ τοῦ Ἰακὼβ ἐπαινουμένη παρὰ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν. τοῦτο λέγει: τὸ σκεῦος τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ δοξάζει. εἶτα τί λέγει; Καὶ ἦν ποταμὸς ἕλκων ἐκ δεξιῶν, καὶ ἀνέβαινεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δένδρα ὡραῖα: καὶ ὃς ἂν φάγῃ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι ἡμεῖς μὲν καταβαίνομεν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ γέμοντες ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ ῥύπου, καὶ ἀναβαίνομεν καρποφοροῦντες ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐλπίδα εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ἔχοντες. Καὶ ὃς ἂν φάγῃ ἀπὸ τούτων, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, τοῦτο λέγει: ὃς ἄν, φησίν, ἀκούσῃ τούτων λαλουμένων καὶ πιστεύσῃ, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
pass_a_gloss: Let us seek, if the Lord was concerned to reveal about the water and about the cross. About the water, it is written concerning Israel, how the baptism that brings forgiveness of sins they will not accept, but they will build for themselves. For the prophet says: Be astonished, heaven, and let the earth tremble at this, because this people has done two evil things: they have forsaken me, the spring of life, and they have dug for themselves a pit of death. Is my holy mountain Sinai not a deserted rock? You will be like fledgling birds flying away, having been torn from the nest. And again the prophet says: I will go before you and I will level the mountains and I will shatter the bronze gates and I will break the iron bars, and I will give you hidden, dark, unseen treasures, so that they may know that I am the Lord God. And: You will live in a high, strong rock cave. And: its water is faithful; you will see the king with glory, and your soul will meditate on the fear of the Lord. And again in another prophet it is said: And the one who does these things will be like the tree planted by the waterways, which gives its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and everything that it does will succeed. Not so the wicked, not so, but like the chaff that the wind blows away from the face of the earth. Therefore, the wicked will not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the council of the righteous, because the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the wicked will perish. Notice how the water and the cross have been ordained for the same purpose. For he says: Blessed are those who, having hoped in the cross, went down into the water, because he says the reward will be given in its own time: then, he says, I will repay. Now, what he says: the leaves will not wither, this means: every word that goes out from you through your mouth in faith and love will be for the turning back and hope of many. And again another prophet says: And the land of Jacob was praised above all the earth. This means: the vessel of his Spirit is glorified. Then what does he say? And there was a river flowing from the right, and beautiful trees were coming up from it: and whoever eats from them will live forever. This means that we go down into the water full of sins and filth, and we come up bearing fruit in the heart, the fear and the hope in Jesus, having the Spirit. And whoever eats from these will live forever, this means: whoever, he says, hears these things being spoken and believes, will live forever.
pass_b_english: Let us ask whether the Lord cared to reveal the meaning of the water and the cross. Concerning the water, Scripture speaks about Israel: the baptism that brings forgiveness of sins will not be accepted by them; instead they will build for themselves. The prophet says, "Be astonished, O heavens, and let the earth tremble all the more at this, for this people has committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of life, and dug for themselves a cistern of death" (Jeremiah 2:12–13). "Is my holy mountain Sinai a deserted rock? You will be like fledgling birds flying away, torn from the nest" (Jeremiah 2:14–15 LXX). Again the prophet says, "I will go before you and level the mountains, shatter the bronze gates, break the iron bars, and give you hidden, dark, unseen treasures, so that you may know that I am the Lord God" (Isaiah 45:2–3). And, "You will dwell in a high cave of a strong rock" (Isaiah 33:16). And, "His water is faithful; you will see the king in glory, and your soul will meditate on the fear of the Lord" (Isaiah 33:16–17). In another prophet it says: "The one who does these things will be like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season, and its leaf does not wither; whatever he does prospers. The wicked are not so, but are like chaff that the wind drives away. Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous, for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish" (Psalm 1:3–6). Notice how the water and the cross have been ordained for the same purpose. For he says: "Blessed are those who, having set their hope on the cross, went down into the water, because the reward will be given in its own time: then, he says, I will repay." Now, when he says, "the leaves will not wither," he means: every word that goes out from you through your mouth in faith and love will bring turning back and hope to many. And again another prophet says: "The land of Jacob was praised above all the earth" (Ezekiel 20:6 LXX). This means: the vessel of his Spirit is glorified. Then what does he say? "There was a river flowing from the right, and beautiful trees grew up from it; whoever eats from them will live forever" (Ezekiel 47:1, 7, 12 LXX). This means that we go down into the water full of sins and filth, and come up bearing fruit in the heart—fear and hope in Jesus—having the Spirit. And "whoever eats from these will live forever" means: whoever hears these things spoken and believes will live forever.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A preserves the sense of all clauses, and Pass B provides accurate English with appropriate scripture citations (Jeremiah, Isaiah, Psalms, Ezekiel) that match the quoted content. The title 'Baptism and the Cross' correctly names the thought of the chapter.
